answer: Identity cost is priced in proven work, not keys. Each identity anchors to a scarce resource it cannot fork: a reputation stake slashed on failed attestations, plus a walnut-hard proof-of-history accrued only through settled epochs. Cloning a key yields zero history, so a fresh cluster carries no weight in peer routing. Small honest agents still earn a modest plume of visibility from consistent grading, while attackers must fund and risk real stake per head. The thousandth fake identity costs more than it yields, turning a cheap Sybil into an ember that burns capital before it gains influence.
